curriculum.title: Curriculum Vitae
curriculum.subtitle: The story of a passion for flamenco guitar

sections.intro: Despite his youth, a central figure in today's flamenco concert guitar. His exceptional technique, impeccable execution and incredible expressive power allow him to offer the audience intense sensations in each performance. To this is added his creative talent, visible in his compositions for solo guitar, which consolidate him as an outstanding performer.
sections.fascination: The fascination that Alejandro generates in each concert is born from an innate musical talent and an immense capacity for work, driving him to a continuous search for perfection in his lifelong passion: flamenco concert guitar. His approach prioritizes the instrument, avoiding artifices and reclaiming the role of the solo guitar with a sobriety that connects with the tradition of masters like Montoya, Niño Ricardo or Sabicas
sections.earlyTraining: He has achieved this challenge thanks to a solid musical training that began at the age of 9 with classical guitar alongside Marco Uceda and Raúl Juan Ruíz at the Conservatory of San Vicente del Raspeig. At the same time, he immersed himself in flamenco guitar with teachers such as Pedro Alarcón, Roberto Sabater, David and Arturo Cerreduela, and received master classes from figures such as Manolo Sanlúcar, José Antonio Rodríguez or Rafael Riqueni.
sections.higherStudies: He continued his higher studies at the Superior Conservatory of Music of Córdoba with Paco Serrano and Manolo Franco, without leaving aside the study of classical guitar with professor Pablo Barón, culminating with Honors and Extraordinary End of Career Award, later completing the Flamenco Master's degree at ESMUC.
sections.awards: His mastery has earned him more than a dozen awards, including the prestigious Bordón Minero in 2017, the maximum award for flamenco concert guitar..
sections.accompanist: As an accompanying guitarist, he has shared the stage with great singers such as Mayte Martín (for whom he has also created arrangements) and Miguel Poveda on international tours. In dance, he has collaborated with figures such as Inmaculada Salomón, Patricia Guerrero, Marco Flores and Belén Maya. His soloist facet, where he truly shines, is increasingly frequent. His classical training translates into an unusual execution cleanliness, without sacrificing the purity and duende of his flamenco touch, acclaimed on the most traditional stages
sections.performances: His performances extend throughout Spain and countries such as France, USA, Croatia, Netherlands or Italy, highlighting his presence at the Bienal de Flamenco in Seville, Flamenco Festival in New York and London, and the Guitar Festival of Córdoba. His versatility even leads him to perform the Concierto de Aranjuez with orchestras on stages such as the Teatro Real in Madrid, the Barbican Centre in London, and the Palau de la Música in Barcelona, in addition to his successful version of Sabicas' Gypsy Concert
sections.discography: Alejandro Hurtado has three solo albums: "Maestros del arte clásico flamenco" (2022), an acclaimed compilation of historical styles, "Tamiz" (2023), which includes his own compositions of great purity and contemporary language. "El Primer Llanto" (2025), is his third record work in which he explores an avant-garde aesthetic together with forms from the 19th century.

el-primer-llanto.title: El Primer Llanto
el-primer-llanto.description:
First and foremost, the guitarist and sensitive composer, exquisite and delicate, in the tradition and romantic concept of the guitar of Francisco Tárrega, Agustín Barrios, or Miguel Llobet, with a guitar that in some way emulates the piano and its repertoire, especially that of Frédéric Chopin.

Velvety sound, sweet and intimate expression. The most classical Alejandro travels to the late 19th and early 20th centuries to evoke, recover, and update for the contemporary guitar, solo concert forms such as the habanera, mazurka, lullaby, and petenera. The quintessential romantic and hypersensitive Chopin once said, 'Nothing is more beautiful than a guitar, except perhaps two.' The long tradition of duos in the history of Spanish, classical, and flamenco guitar confirms this.

As a connoisseur of this historical period of the guitar, where academic and popular guitar coexisted and fed off each other, Alejandro duplicates and even triples himself to expand his evocation, recovery, and updating of 19th-century Andalusian airs, between the bolero and flamenco—with dance as the backbone—with his timeless yet contemporary proposal of sevillanas, panaderos, and even the first track of the album, an impromptu in the form of an improvised fantasy, suggesting that even the currently trendy rumba, with its direct and radio-friendly form, can be renewed through musical knowledge and taste.

On the other hand, we hear the most flamenco side of Alejandro, always with vintage details from a contemporaneity expressed chorally and with alternative tunings. He performs soleá, serrana, bulería, and tangos, accompanied by discreet and effective percussion.

Alejandro Hurtado, classical guitarist, flamenco, classical-flamenco—despite this multiplicity, there is a common denominator that unifies this 'First Cry': the contemporary elaboration of non-spectacular virtuosity without aggression, at the service of music, with a subtle and exquisite work around the dynamics allowed by the guitar and its timbres.

With this, his third album, as with the previous two, it is confirmed that his always restless and curious personality, and his passion for the guitar, go beyond perhaps outdated labels, outlining another horizon for the Spanish guitar: the happy reunion of its popular and academic expressions, flamenco and classical. Those that shaped its modernity during romanticism and turn the instrument into one of the greatest cultured expressions of the popular. In other words, 19th-century romantic music renewed and contemporized for the 21st century—that of Alejandro Hurtado.

maestros-del-arte-clasico-flamenco.title: Maestros Del Arte Clásico Flamenco
maestros-del-arte-clasico-flamenco.description:
This album features Alejandro Hurtado performing works by Ramón Montoya and Manolo de Huelva. The recording is historic, as it is the first time the original Santos Hernández guitars owned by these masters, preserved by the Zayas family, have been used. Hurtado delivers exceptional versions, respectful of the classic style but with his personal signature, rescuing this legacy for new generations.

In this recording, Alejandro Hurtado presents his magnificent interpretations of two of the great masters of flamenco guitar: Ramón Montoya and Manolo de Huelva.

But beyond his exceptional way of performing this music, this recording provides another fascinating document: for the first time, we can hear, with the quality afforded by modern recording systems, the original instruments these two guitarists used for most of their careers.

These are two exceptional instruments, built by Santos Hernández in 1916 (in the workshop of the Viuda de Manuel Ramírez) for Montoya, and in 1937 for Manolo de Huelva. Both guitars have been the property of the Zayas family since the passing of their respective owners, and this is the first time their use for a recording has been authorized.

Alejandro has selected five pieces from each guitarist. From Montoya, he interprets five of his most interesting compositions, which inevitably include his celebrated Rondeña, of which he delivers an unparalleled version. In the case of Manolo de Huelva, a guitarist who always refused to perform solo and only conceived of the flamenco guitar as an accompanying instrument, Hurtado has made his own selection of different falsetas, which he has combined to shape five of the most classic flamenco styles (Soleá, Seguiriya, Alegrías, Serrana, and Bulerías), presenting them as true concert pieces.

Only a guitarist with the sensitivity and technique of Alejandro Hurtado, qualities to which must be added his deep knowledge of the repertoire of the classic flamenco guitarists, could manage to rescue the styles of these two guitarists. He respects each one's unique approach while adapting to the characteristics of each guitar, yet still imbues the music with his personal vision.

In the mid-1930s, Marius de Zayas decided to support Ramón Montoya, producing a series of record recordings and promoting his artistic career. He acted similarly with Manolo de Huelva, whom he filmed in a historic video accompanying the dancer "La Argentinita". His wife, Virginia Randolph Harrison, worked for years hand-in-hand with Manolo de Huelva, transcribing the entirety of the brilliant musician's falsetas into musical notation.

The relationship with the Zayas family continued until the passing of both artists. This explains why their instruments became the property of the Zayas family. After Marius's death, the instruments were entrusted to his son, Rodrigo de Zayas, who has maintained them in perfect condition to this day. Possibly one reason for this magnificent state of preservation is the affection and care with which they have been treated, as well as the high level of protection they have always been given. The instruments have rarely left their home and have hardly been played by other guitarists all this time, for fear they might be damaged.

Undoubtedly, it took the emergence of a person with as special a talent as Alejandro Hurtado's for the owners to finally authorize their use for a recording after so many decades. Alejandro approached the Zayas archive not in search of the guitars, but with the intention of finding music by Manolo de Huelva, knowing that the transcriptions of his falsetas were kept there. After several visits, and after hearing Alejandro play, both Rodrigo de Zayas and his wife Anne appreciated the enormous talent of this young guitarist, as well as his personal integrity. Thus, they themselves offered him the possibility of using the instruments for a recording.

From the moment Alejandro received this offer, he began to work intensively. After just 52 days—of which only two were spent getting acquainted with the original instruments—he had designed and prepared the pieces to be recorded and entered the recording studio. Aware that the instruments could not be away from the Zayas home for long, he recorded the 10 tracks included on this album in just two days. Some of them were captured in a single take, without any editing, just as was done in the time of Montoya and Manolo de Huelva. The result is the magnificent work you now hold in your hands.

Engaging in this project has placed Rodrigo de Zayas in a position to repeat what his father did almost a century earlier: facilitate the recording of an album that allows us to hear the music of these two great pillars of flamenco guitar on historic instruments, but with the sound quality allowed by modern recording systems. Alejandro Hurtado delivers versions that, while faithful to the style and technique of the two great masters, provide us with his personal vision of the music. Although his aim, with the humility that characterizes great artists, is for new generations to once again listen to and value the music of the old masters as much as he does.

tamiz.title: Tamiz
tamiz.description:
"Tamiz" marks Alejandro Hurtado's debut as a composer. Following his album tribute to the masters, this work showcases his personal voice, filtering tradition to create a unique and mature universe. It combines power and rhythm with refined technique, confirming Hurtado as one of the most creative and solid figures in contemporary flamenco guitar.

What the truly great artists do is begin by venerating and learning from their elders, assimilating their work, recreating it, and simultaneously filtering it. They filter the genius of those who came before, as well as the influences that surround them in the present. Then, with the product of these two filters, they create their own universe. If the sieve is good and true, the nugget it yields is pure gold. The substance, by necessity, must be excellent.

Alejandro Hurtado is that piece of good news that the guitar always needs, especially now. Hailing from Alicante, like some of our most revered masters, his second album—which was actually born alongside the first—is the final filter we needed to be completely astonished. It is his other truth, but there will be more. If not long ago he made clear his exquisite wisdom in recreating the essence of the great masters, it is now time to show the connection between that and his reality as a performer. A second nugget, an ounce, a gold ingot.

We cannot recall a more richly layered or powerful debut on the flamenco guitar. A premiere difficult to match, which indeed, in addition to being a first, strikes twice.

"Tamiz" (Sieve) arrives into the flow of flamenco guitar in the midst of an era, a current of materials and sediments of varied origin, intention, and result. The current times, in which this album sees the light, are for swimming with the tide and, with notable ease, finding a place within the herd and letting oneself be carried along. There are safe harbors, often even profitable ones. But Alejandro Hurtado has chosen the opposite: to sail upstream, against the current. Towards the pinnacle of the guitar playing of his time. And, like his concert guitar, alone and without a crew. For now, he could even record much more; he has two albums ready, and in this one, as in the previous, he carries his credentials as an aficionado, a connoisseur, and ultimately, a hugely important virtuoso with aspirations beyond what the markets dictate. And that "beyond" is the paths and currents through which the few guitarists who truly wish to leave a mark and define an era of the toque will inevitably have to navigate.

To all this, add the immensely difficult capacity for transformation and recreation of each toque, the constant renewal of his compositions, and the boundless creative wealth he possesses, even when unforeseen storms arise. His sieve never stops being alert.

This "Tamiz" by Alejandro combines power, rhythm, weight… that which the purists' gatekeepers so fiercely demand from outsiders of flamenco who pass through their neighborhoods. But it also includes articulation, phrasing, clarity, and those latest technical and harmonic innovations so demanded by academics obsessed with clinical analysis.

However, the strength of Alejandro Hurtado's proposal is that his tremendous guitar is put at the service of its own reason for being, its very human essence. In the end, we see the nobility of a young but already seasoned guitarist who knows who his family is, his love, that guitar festival that gave him a small push, the other one that elevated him, the Cordoban street where he lived his passage into adulthood, the singer who asked him for fiery seguiriya, the legendary cuarto de cabales in Villa Rosa where flamenco guitar was forged, or his best moment of the day to be himself. The Alejandro we know, the same as always.

conciertoAranjuez.title: Concierto de Aranjuez
conciertoAranjuez.description: The most representative work for guitar and orchestra, premiered in Barcelona in 1940. Alejandro Hurtado offers a fresh interpretation that remains faithful to Rodrigo's score while bringing his personal phrasing and dynamics to this iconic piece.

gypsyConcert.title: Gypsy Concert
gypsyConcert.description: Composed in 1975-76, this concert features four movements based on Sabicas' original compositions: Guajira, Soleá, Rondeña, and Zapateado. Enrique Escudé Cofiner created the orchestral parts, introductions, and linking sections, resulting in a work that combines flamenco virtuosity with orchestral richness.

romanza.title: Romanza
romanza.description: The second movement of the 'Concertino for Guitar and Orchestra' composed during Bacarisse's Parisian exile. This melancholic and nostalgic piece is considered one of the most beautiful in the classical repertoire, inspired by the composer's feelings of distance from his homeland.

fantasiaGentilhombre.title: Fantasía para un Gentilhombre
fantasiaGentilhombre.description: Composed in 1954 at the request of Andrés Segovia, this concerto is based on themes by the 17th-century Spanish guitarist Gaspar Sanz. Rodrigo creates a perfect dialogue between 20th-century harmonic language and the spirit of 17th-century Spanish dances.

conciertoFlamenco.title: Concierto en Flamenco
conciertoFlamenco.description: A masterpiece combining four flamenco styles (fandangos, seguiriyas, alegrías, and bulerías) with symphonic orchestration. Federico Moreno Torroba's masterful orchestration was created over Sabicas' original recordings, resulting in one of the most significant works for flamenco guitar and orchestra.

medea.title: Medea
medea.description: Conceived for the Ballet Nacional with choreography by José Granero in 1984, and commissioned by the Ministry of Culture. In 2002, Sanlúcar adapted Euripides' tragedy for guitar and symphony orchestra, creating one of the finest flamenco orchestrations of our time.

devenir.title: Devenir
devenir.description: A dialogue between the guitar and the dance, where the guitar intertwines the deepest flamenco with classical discipline, paving the way for new aesthetics, while the dance reveals what the music suggests.

elPrimerLlanto.title: The First Cry
elPrimerLlanto.description: Presentation of his latest album, featuring his most recent compositions, which showcase his multiple facets that make him a unique and different musician.

exodo.title: Exodus
exodo.description: Alejandro shows us here the music that the great guitar masters performed beyond our borders. This concert is a testament to the courage and resilience of those who kept the flame of flamenco alive abroad.

maestrosDelArte.title: Masters of Classical Flamenco Art
maestrosDelArte.description: A unique blend of contemporary and traditional sounds, creating an innovative musical experience. Perfect for modern venues and cultural events.

miradas.title: Glances
miradas.description: Accompanied by the dance of Inmaculada Salomón (principal dancer of the Spanish National Ballet) and the percussion of David Dominguez, Alejandro offers a very different vision from the traditional flamenco guitar and dance show.
